stem: The facial nerve exits the posterior cranial fossa through which of the following:
fact: The facial nerve enters the internal acoustic meatus before continuing into the facial canal.
mnemonic: VII travels with VIII through the internal acoustic meatus.
finding: CN VII exits the posterior cranial fossa via the internal acoustic meatus.

stem: A 54 year old man presents to ED complaining of difficulty chewing. On examination, you note he has loss of muscle bulk over the masseter muscle and loss of power opening the jaw. He also has loss of tactile sensation involving the anterior two thirds of the tongue. Which of the following cranial nerves is most likely affected:
fact: V3 supplies the muscles of mastication and general sensation from the anterior two-thirds of the tongue through the lingual nerve.
mnemonic: V3 moves the jaw and feels the front tongue.
finding: The mandibular division provides motor mastication and anterior tongue general sensation.

stem: Regarding the mandibular nerve, which of the following statements is INCORRECT:
options: The mandibular nerve enters the infratemporal fossa between the tensor veli palatini muscle and the lateral pterygoid muscle.
The mandibular nerve exits the cranium through the foramen ovale.
The mandibular nerve supplies sensation to the anterior two-thirds of the tongue.
The mandibular nerve innervates the orbicularis oculi.
The mandibular nerve has both motor and sensory function.
fact: Orbicularis oculi is a muscle of facial expression supplied by the facial nerve, not V3.
mnemonic: V3 chews; VII closes the eyelids.
finding: V3 is mixed and exits through foramen ovale, but orbicularis oculi is supplied by CN VII.

stem: Regarding the oculomotor nerve, which of the following statements is CORRECT:
options: The oculomotor nerve has both motor and sensory function.
The oculomotor nerve innervates all of the extraocular muscles.
The oculomotor nerve innervates the dilator pupillae muscle.
The oculomotor nerve passes through the lateral part of the cavernous sinus.
The oculomotor nerve enters the orbit through the optic canal.
fact: CN III passes through the lateral cavernous sinus and enters the orbit via the superior orbital fissure.
mnemonic: III travels in the cavernous sinus, then superior fissure.
finding: The oculomotor nerve reference supports lateral cavernous-sinus passage.

stem: A 29 year old man has sustained a significant head injury. On examination it is noted that his uvula is deviated to the right. Which of the following nerves is most likely affected:
fact: A unilateral vagus lesion causes palatal weakness and uvular deviation away from the affected side.
mnemonic: Vagus weakness pulls the uvula away.
finding: Left vagus palsy produces uvular deviation to the right.

stem: The mandibular division of the trigeminal nerve supplies general sensation to all of the following regions EXCEPT for the:
fact: The upper lip is supplied by infraorbital branches of V2, not the mandibular division.
finding: The maxillary division supplies upper-lip sensation.

stem: Regarding the vagus nerve, which of the following statements is CORRECT:
options: It exits the skull through the foramen ovale.
It carries general sensation from the oropharynx.
It carries visceral afferent fibres from the aortic arch baroreceptors.
It carries parasympathetic fibres to the parotid gland.
It is the afferent nerve of the gag reflex.
fact: The vagus carries visceral afferent information from the aortic arch, including baroreceptor input.
finding: The vagus reference supports aortic-arch visceral afferents.

stem: The maxillary nerve supplies general sensation to all of the following regions EXCEPT for the:
fact: The maxillary division does not supply general sensation to the external ear.
mnemonic: V2 covers midface, palate, teeth, and upper lip, not the ear.
finding: External-ear sensation is not a maxillary-division territory.

stem: A 45 year old lady presents to ED with right sided facial weakness. Your consultant suspects a facial nerve palsy. Which of the following clinical features would you most likely see on examination:
options: Loss of tactile sensation to anterior two-thirds of tongue
Loss of sensation to right side of the face
fact: Facial-nerve palsy can cause hyperacusis through stapedius weakness.
mnemonic: VII protects the stapedius from loudness.
finding: CN VII supplies stapedius; palsy can produce hyperacusis.

stem: A 56 year old female presents to ED complaining of loss of sensation over the anterior two-thirds of her tongue. Taste and salivation are intact. Which of the following nerves is most likely affected:
fact: The lingual nerve carries general sensation from the anterior two-thirds of the tongue; chorda tympani carries taste and secretomotor fibres.
mnemonic: Lingual feels; chorda tastes and secretes.
finding: The lingual-nerve reference supports isolated anterior-tongue general sensory loss.
